front: Forms of acceleration in a straight line
Acceleration given as a function of displacement x
back: Use $v\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} = f(x)$: $\int v\,\mathrm{d}v = \int f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$ gives $\tfrac{1}{2}v^2$ in terms of $x$.

front: Acceleration given as a function of time t
back: Integrate with respect to t for v, again for x; fix each constant from the initial conditions.

front: Resistance depending on v: which form?
back: Time asked → m dv/dt = F(v); distance asked → mv dv/dx = F(v). Separate the variables.
The limiting speed at which the resultant force (and acceleration) is zero, e.g. driving force = resistance.
Opposes motion: enters Newton's law as $-kv$ or $-kv^2$ when the positive direction is the direction of motion.
$\mathbf{v} = \dot{\mathbf{r}}$, $\mathbf{a} = \ddot{\mathbf{r}}$ component by component; integrate components with constant vectors from initial conditions; $\mathbf{F} = m\mathbf{a}$.
suvat assumes constant acceleration; a force depending on t, x or v gives a variable acceleration.
